Subject: Intermittent timeouts this morning - Hosted API p99 spike

Hi Redwood Support,

Request IDs attached (trace-9f3a-req.log). This is impacting payment confirmation flows for a subset of customers. Can you confirm whether this was an infra event or a model change on your side?

Thanks,
Aisha

Date: 2027-06-18T09:05:00Z
From: monica_patel@redwood.com
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.com
Subject: Fwd: Incident - p99 tail during autoscale (Finovate)

Forwarding customer report. Quick notes from SRE: we saw repeated scale-up operations in the GPU pool at 07:35–08:10 PDT. The serving runtime spun up new containers and pulled model shards; cold KV cache and delayed JIT/compilation on a subset of nodes produced high tail latency.

SRE's immediate asks: 1) temporarily pin Finovate traffic to warm pool nodes; 2) enable pre-warm policy for lumen-13b for high-traffic customers; 3) investigate prioritized kernel selection to reduce first-token times.

I'm pulling together a mitigation playbook and will coordinate with sales/CS. Can you weigh in on customer comms and any credit/contract implications?

—Monica
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
Date: 2027-06-18T09:22:00Z
From: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
To: monica_patel@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Subject: Re: Fwd: Incident - p99 tail during autoscale (Finovate)

Thanks — forcing Finovate onto warm nodes is a good short-term mitigation. Lauren: please draft an ASAP note to Aisha explaining what happened and the temporary routing change. Mark: can you confirm capacity for pre-warm for lumen-13b and estimated incremental cost? We need to be decisive — this is an enterprise customer with revenue at risk.

Also, set up a quick post-incident review; include kernel selection and the runtime's behavior under concurrent shard pulls. We should capture: the timeline, how many scale-ups, which instances showed long model load times, and whether KV-cache warmup strategy failed.

- Sean

Date: 2027-06-18T12:45:00Z

To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@finovate.com>
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Subject: Temporary routing & next steps (Finovate incident)

Hi Aisha — apologies for the disruption this morning. Short update: we routed Finovate production traffic to a set of pre-warmed GPU nodes in us-west-2 and applied a temporary request smoothing policy to reduce concurrent scale-ups. Early metrics show p95 down to ~0.8s and p99 below 3s for the affected routes.

We will:
- Keep this routing in place until we've validated a pre-warm profile for lumen-13b (~48 hours).
- Share a technical RCA and mitigation plan by EOD tomorrow.
- Offer a one-time service credit given the impact while we stabilize.

Would you be available for a 30-min postmortem call 06/19 at 09:00 PT?

Thanks for flagging this — we'll follow up with the postmortem and action items.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
Date: 2027-06-20T17:05:00Z
From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Cc: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@finovate.com>
Subject: Post-incident summary: scale-up tail causing p99 regressions — Finovate

Summary (incident window: 2027-06-18T07:33–08:11 PDT):
- Root cause: concurrent autoscale-driven model shard pulls + JIT compilation spikes on a subset of GPU node types. Several nodes pulled full model weights (lumen-13b) into memory while still servicing requests which caused queuing and long first-token times. KV cache coldness amplified the tail.
- Impact: p95 increased to 3.2s and p99 to ~14s for ~420 requests; ~2.3% of Finovate's requests hit 5xx/timeout.
- Immediate mitigations applied: pinned Finovate traffic to pre-warmed nodes, request smoothing (max concurrency per client), and temporary model-pull rate limit. Observed p95/p99 improvement within 20 minutes.
- Long-term actions: (1) implement pre-warm profiles for high-volume customers (timeline: 2 weeks), (2) prioritize kernel selection path for first-token latency (timeline: 3 weeks), (3) add autoscale hysteresis to avoid rapid repeated spin-ups, (4) improve KV-cache pre-population during scale-up.

Attachments: mitigation-action-plan.md (action items & owner matrix). We've proposed a one-time service credit and scheduled the customer postmortem on 2027-06-19 09:00 PT.

I'll sync with finance on credits and with product on rollout priority. Happy to brief execs if you want a short summary slide.

—Markus
Director, Serving Runtime Engineering

Attachment: mitigation-action-plan.md
